title: Children's Online Safety Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete privacy checklist to protect your child online. COPPA compliance, parental controls, safe browsing, and screen time management.
intro: Protecting your child's privacy online requires multiple layers of security. This comprehensive checklist covers everything from COPPA-compliant settings to parental controls and safe browsing practices to keep your kids safe online.

items.task: Install a privacy-focused browser like Incognito Browser
items.why: Regular browsers collect extensive data on users, including children. Privacy browsers block trackers and ads that can expose kids to inappropriate content.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser or similar privacy browser. Set it as the default browser and enable all privacy protection features. Disable data collection and location sharing.

items.task: Enable SafeSearch on all search engines
items.why: Prevents children from accidentally finding inappropriate content through search results, including explicit images and harmful websites.
items.howTo: Go to Google, Bing, and Yahoo search settings. Turn on SafeSearch strict filtering. Lock the setting with your account to prevent changes.

items.task: Set strong passwords and PINs on all devices
items.why: Prevents unauthorized access and ensures parental control settings cannot be easily bypassed by children or others.
items.howTo: Use complex passwords with numbers, letters, and symbols. Enable device lock screens with PINs. Never share admin passwords with children.

items.task: Enable automatic security updates
items.why: Security patches protect against new threats and vulnerabilities that could expose children's data or allow unauthorized access.
items.howTo: Turn on automatic updates in device settings for operating system, browsers, and all apps. Check monthly that updates are installing properly.

items.task: Create separate child user accounts with restricted privileges
items.why: Limits children's ability to install software, change settings, or access inappropriate content while maintaining your admin control.
items.howTo: Create standard (non-admin) accounts for each child. Set up content filters and time restrictions. Regularly review account activity and permissions.

items.task: Configure router-level content filtering
items.why: Provides network-wide protection that can't be easily bypassed, blocking inappropriate sites across all connected devices in your home.
items.howTo: Access your router's admin panel. Enable DNS filtering using services like OpenDNS or CleanBrowsing. Set content categories to block and create device-specific rules.

items.task: Set up screen time limits and schedules
items.why: Prevents internet addiction, ensures adequate sleep, and creates healthy boundaries around device usage for better family balance.
items.howTo: Use built-in screen time controls (iOS Screen Time, Android Digital Wellbeing) or third-party apps. Set daily limits, bedtime restrictions, and app-specific time limits.

items.task: Review and restrict app permissions
items.why: Many apps request unnecessary access to camera, microphone, location, and contacts, potentially exposing children's personal information.
items.howTo: Go through each app's permissions in device settings. Disable location, camera, microphone access unless absolutely necessary. Remove unused apps regularly.

items.task: Enable purchase restrictions and require approval
items.why: Prevents accidental or unauthorized purchases, protects payment information, and gives parents control over what content children can access.
items.howTo: Turn on purchase approval in app stores. Remove stored payment methods from child accounts. Set up family sharing with purchase notifications.

items.task: Enable YouTube Restricted Mode or use YouTube Kids
items.why: Filters out potentially mature content and reduces exposure to inappropriate videos, comments, and advertising targeted at adults.
items.howTo: Turn on Restricted Mode in YouTube settings or download YouTube Kids app. Create supervised accounts and review watch history regularly.

items.task: Configure gaming platform parental controls
items.why: Gaming platforms often have chat features, user-generated content, and online interactions that can expose children to inappropriate behavior.
items.howTo: Set up parental controls on PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, Steam, etc. Disable chat with strangers, limit online interactions, and set content ratings.

items.task: Verify your child meets minimum age requirements for platforms
items.why: COPPA requires platforms to get parental consent for children under 13. Many platforms have minimum age requirements for safety reasons.
items.howTo: Check platform terms of service for age requirements. Don't allow children to lie about their age when creating accounts. Use kid-specific alternatives when available.

items.task: Set social media accounts to maximum privacy
items.why: Prevents strangers from contacting your child, seeing their posts, or gathering personal information that could be used for harmful purposes.
items.howTo: Make profiles private, disable location sharing, turn off friend suggestions, and require approval for followers/friend requests. Disable data sharing with third parties.

items.task: Limit who can contact your child online
items.why: Reduces risk of contact from predators, cyberbullies, or strangers who might try to manipulate or harm your child.
items.howTo: Set messaging to friends-only, disable comments from strangers, turn off video calling with unknown contacts, and review contact lists regularly.

items.task: Disable location sharing and geotagging
items.why: Location data can reveal where your child lives, goes to school, or spends time, creating safety risks and privacy concerns.
items.howTo: Turn off location services for social apps, disable geotagging on photos, and review location history settings. Teach children not to share location information.

items.task: Monitor friend lists and online connections
items.why: Helps identify potential risks from strangers or inappropriate contacts while maintaining awareness of your child's online social circle.
items.howTo: Regularly review friend/follower lists, ask about new online friends, and maintain open communication about who your child interacts with online.

items.task: Educate children about protecting personal information
items.why: Children often overshare personal details that can be used for identity theft, stalking, or other harmful purposes by malicious actors.
items.howTo: Teach children never to share full names, addresses, phone numbers, school names, or family details online. Create family rules about information sharing.

items.task: Opt out of data collection and advertising tracking
items.why: Companies collect extensive data on children for advertising and profiling, which violates COPPA principles and can impact their future privacy.
items.howTo: Disable ad personalization, opt out of data sharing in app settings, and use privacy tools that block tracking. Review privacy policies for child-focused apps.

items.task: Control photo and video sharing permissions
items.why: Images can contain metadata, be misused by others, or expose private information about your family and home environment.
items.howTo: Teach children to ask permission before posting photos, disable automatic photo syncing, and review photo sharing settings on all platforms regularly.

items.task: Set up monitoring for your child's name and information online
items.why: Early detection of identity theft, inappropriate content featuring your child, or unauthorized account creation in their name.
items.howTo: Set up Google Alerts for your child's name, monitor their digital footprint monthly, and check for unauthorized social media accounts or posts.

items.task: Secure cloud storage and backup accounts
items.why: Cloud accounts often contain photos, documents, and personal information that need protection from unauthorized access or data breaches.
items.howTo: Enable two-factor authentication on cloud accounts, review sharing permissions, and ensure only authorized family members have access to shared storage.

pro_tips: Have regular 'digital check-ins' with your children to discuss their online experiences and any concerns they might have encountered.
Use family media agreements that clearly outline rules and expectations for internet use, signed by both parents and children.
Consider using separate email addresses for different purposes - one for school, one for family communication, and avoid using real names in usernames.
Test your parental controls regularly by trying to access blocked content to ensure they're working properly and haven't been bypassed.
Stay informed about new apps and platforms your children's friends are using, as popular platforms change frequently and have different safety features.
